record.paper_title: Results and Open Problems in Mathematical General Relativity
record.original_question: Given initial data on a Cauchy hypersurface that satisfy the Einstein constraint equations, does the corresponding maximal globally hyperbolic solution of the Einstein equations exist globally to the future, in the geometric sense that all future-directed causal geodesics are complete?

evidence.quote: For the mathematician the question is of the future global existence of a solution of the Einstein equations, starting from initial data.
“Global” is usually taken as “completeness of causal — that is timelike or null — geodesics”.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(\Sigma, g, K)$ be a smooth initial data set for the vacuum Einstein equations, where $\Sigma$ is a 3-dimensional manifold, $g$ is a Riemannian metric on $\Sigma$, and $K$ is a symmetric $(0,2)$-tensor field on $\Sigma$ representing the second fundamental form, satisfying the Einstein vacuum constraint equations
$$R(g) - |K|_g^2 + (\mathrm{tr}_g K)^2 = 0, \qquad \mathrm{div}_g K - d(\mathrm{tr}_g K) = 0,$$
where $R(g)$ denotes the scalar curvature of $g$. By the theorem of Choquet-Bruhat and Geroch, there exists a unique (up to isometry) maximal globally hyperbolic development $(\mathcal{M}, \mathbf{g})$ of $(\Sigma, g, K)$, namely a smooth Lorentzian 4-manifold $(\mathcal{M}, \mathbf{g})$ solving $\mathrm{Ric}(\mathbf{g}) = 0$ such that $\Sigma$ embeds into $\mathcal{M}$ as a Cauchy hypersurface inducing the data $(g, K)$, and which is maximal among all such globally hyperbolic developments.

Determine necessary and/or sufficient conditions on $(\Sigma, g, K)$ that guarantee future geodesic completeness of the maximal globally hyperbolic development; equivalently, determine for which initial data sets every future-directed causal (timelike or null) geodesic in $(\mathcal{M}, \mathbf{g})$ can be extended to arbitrarily large values of an affine parameter.
artifact.status_search_result: The general question is open. Future causal geodesic completeness has been established in several important restricted regimes: stability of Minkowski space (Christodoulou–Klainerman, and later Lindblad–Rodnianski) for small asymptotically flat perturbations of Minkowski data; Friedrich's nonlinear stability of de Sitter space for small perturbations with positive cosmological constant; future asymptotic simplicity and null completeness for small hyperboloidal data; and various symmetry-reduced classes (e.g., polarized $T^2$-symmetric, surface symmetric expanding cosmologies). For general (large, far-from-CMC, or low-symmetry) initial data, future completeness is a major open problem, intimately tied to weak cosmic censorship.

status_evidence.title: Theorems on Existence and Global Dynamics for the Einstein Equations
status_evidence.snippet: For spatially compact spacetimes that expand indefinitely, whether the spacetime is causally geodesically complete towards the future is natural to pose but very difficult to prove.
status_evidence.claim: General future completeness is recognized as a hard, largely open problem; only restricted classes have been resolved.

status_evidence.title: Future asymptotics and geodesic completeness of polarized T2-symmetric spacetimes
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes future geodesic completeness within the polarized T^2-symmetric class.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist under symmetry assumptions.

status_evidence.title: On the existence of n-geodesically complete or future complete solutions of Einstein's field equations
status_evidence.snippet: Friedrich's results on future complete solutions with smooth asymptotic structure for hyperboloidal data near Minkowski.
status_evidence.claim: Small-data stability results give future completeness in restricted regimes.
